lines.name: Red Line
lines.summary: The backbone of Dubai: driverless trains along Sheikh Zayed Road from Centrepoint to Life Pharmacy, with the Route 2020 branch to Expo City Dubai.
facts: First urban metro on the Arabian Peninsula (9 Sept 2009)
Route 2020 branch to Expo City opened in 2021
About 74 minutes from Centrepoint to Expo City Dubai

lines.name: Green Line
lines.summary: Loops through old Dubai under the Creek, from e& in Al Qusais to Creek in Al Jaddaf.
facts: Al Jadaf and Creek stations added in March 2014
Interchanges with the Red Line at Union and BurJuman

lines.name: Blue Line
lines.summary: A Y-shaped line linking Creek and Centrepoint to International City, Dubai Silicon Oasis and Academic City, crossing Dubai Creek on a 1.3 km bridge.
facts: About 25% complete in September 2026; tunnelling began May 2026
15.5 km underground, 14.5 km elevated
Dubai Creek Harbour station designed by SOM, about 74 m tall
AED 20.5 billion contract awarded December 2024

lines.name: Gold Line
lines.summary: A fully underground line from Al Ghubaiba to Jumeirah Golf Estates through Al Satwa, City Walk, Business Bay, Meydan and Al Barsha South.
facts: Approved 22 April 2026, AED 34 billion
18 stations; RTA has not published their locations, so only confirmed interchanges are shown
Projected 465,000 riders a day beyond 2040

lines.name: Dubai Tram
lines.summary: Catenary-free tram through Al Sufouh, Dubai Marina and JBR, looping at the Marina end.
facts: Ground-level power supply, no overhead wires
Interchanges with the Red Line at DMCC and Sobha Realty, and the Palm Monorail at Palm Jumeirah

lines.name: Palm Monorail
lines.summary: Runs up the trunk of Palm Jumeirah from Palm Gateway to Atlantis Aquaventure.
facts: The Middle East's first monorail (April 2009)
Suspended December 2025, back in service June 2026

lines.name: Etihad Rail passenger
lines.summary: The UAE's first national passenger trains, opening in phases from June 2026 on the Etihad Rail network: Abu Dhabi to Dubai and Fujairah first, then Al Dhafra and Sharjah.
facts: Abu Dhabi to Dubai in 57 minutes; Abu Dhabi to Fujairah in 1 h 45
Up to 200 km/h; about 400 seats per train
Dubai's Al Yalayis station links to Jumeirah Golf Estates metro by a 400 m footbridge

lines.name: Etihad Rail network
lines.summary: The 900 km standard-gauge national network from the Saudi border at Ghuwaifat to Fujairah, with branches to Khalifa Port, Jebel Ali, Ras Al Khaimah and the Shah gas field.
facts: Stage 1 (Shah, Habshan, Ruwais) carrying sulphur since 2016
Stage 2 completed the national network in February 2023
Planned to join the GCC Railway at Ghuwaifat

lines.name: High-speed rail
lines.summary: An electrified 350 km/h line linking Abu Dhabi and Dubai in about 30 minutes, separate from the national network.
facts: Announced December 2024; expected to be operational by 2030
Stations: Reem Island, Saadiyat Island, Yas Island, Zayed International Airport, Al Maktoum International Airport, Al Jaddaf
RTA plans show it running roughly along Al Khail Road in Dubai

lines.name: Hafeet Rail
lines.summary: A UAE-Oman line from the Etihad Rail network near Abu Dhabi through Al Ain to the port of Sohar.
facts: About 40% complete in April 2026; track laying under way
Abu Dhabi to Sohar in about 100 minutes, Al Ain to Sohar in 47 minutes
Joint venture of Etihad Rail, Oman Rail and Mubadala
UAE section from OpenStreetMap; the Oman section is drawn as an indicative corridor

lines.name: Abu Dhabi Tram
lines.summary: Line 4: a light rail line from Yas Island across to Al Raha, Etihad Plaza and Zayed International Airport, with later phases to Khalifa City and a Yas loop.
facts: Phase 1: about 20 km and 23 stations; 33 km with later phases
Yas Island to Zayed International Airport in about 20 minutes
Only termini and key stops are shown; the full stop list is not public
